timeline.title: A Short History of Welcoming Babies
items: Families held a party a few days after a birth, when the new baby was carried around the family hearth.
The architect William Kent designed a little carriage for a duke's children. It was pulled by a goat.
Baby showers became popular in America, with friends showering the parents to be with gifts.
Doctors in Glasgow showed how ultrasound could safely see a baby before birth. The scan on the fridge began here.
today: Not in the history books yet. But already the most famous baby in ours.

letters.title: What the World Has Said About Babies
items: Every child begins the world again.
A baby is God's opinion that the world should go on.
Babies are such a nice way to start people.
A new baby is like the beginning of all things: wonder, hope, a dream of possibilities.
letters.hand: They all say it beautifully. We just say: we cannot wait to meet you.

facts.title: The Science of the Bump
items: A baby's heart starts beating at around six weeks, and it beats about twice as fast as a grown up's.
Babies in the womb can hear voices by about 25 weeks. They will know yours when they arrive.
Scans show babies yawning, hiccuping and even smiling before they are born.
Fingerprints form in the womb, months before birth. Nobody else will ever have the same ones.
Many babies are most active in the evening, just when their mum is trying to sleep.
Babies are born with around 300 bones. Some join together as they grow, so adults have 206.
facts.hand: Science can explain a lot. It cannot explain how loved this baby already is.

note.title: What we believe a family is
paras: We make magazines for a living, but some feel different. This was one of them.
We believe the waiting is part of the magic: the scans on the fridge, the names on a list, the tiny clothes folded and refolded, and everyone who loves you counting the days.
{who}, someone wanted you to have something special. Not just another gift for the nursery, but pages full of you, and of the little one on the way.
That someone is {from}. And from everything they told us, this baby is already loved beyond measure.
